text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended mixed in active trading on Tuesday with institutions continuing to dominate market movements, traders said.
The key September 1996 contract ended at an intra-day high of 2,538 yuan ($305) per tonne, rising 22 yuan. It opened at a low of 2,520.
October fell 40 yuan to 2,375 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose sharply to 33,100 tonnes from 1,100.
Traders said individuals had to liquidate their positions with institutional dominating the market which made open interest fall sharply.
The open interest of the September contract fell to 25,670 lots from 27,870. One lot is five tonnes.
"Many stop loss orders from retail investors emerged in the market with the approach of the delivery date, because they don't want to take spot rice," one trader said.
The September contract will begin delivery on September 17.
Analysts said stop loss orders from individuals would surge again in the next few days.
